_about: The register behind /quality/methods (#5918, #5937). One entry per rule, instrument and known gap. Edit here, never in the page. Every number needs a source link; tests/unit/quality-methods.test.ts checks the shape.

rules.rule: Only accuracy against something people made counts as quality. Two models agreeing, or one model giving the same answer twice, is agreement or stability, and we label it so.
Headline rates come from random draws of our own pages. A rate measured on passages chosen because a reference exists describes only those passages.
Sample books, not pages. Pages in one book share a scan, a hand and an engine, so they count as one observation.
Compare two methods only on the same pages. Every comparison includes a run of a method against itself, to show how much changes by chance, and planted errors the judge must catch.
Write down what result would change our practice before reading any results, with a margin for chance.
An AI judge is an instrument under test. It is checked on the exact task, with planted errors that look like real ones, before its verdicts are used.
Where people have already typed a text and released it openly, we use their text rather than a machine reading, and the page image stays beside it so it can be checked.
What we cannot read reliably, we hold back rather than publish: a reading below its bar, a script with no tested reader, a page the pipeline cannot see.

Every serious finding is closed by something that lasts: a test page that every later change must pass, an entry on the improvement board with an owner, and, for a book that is broken or not ours to publish, hiding it the same day. A detector's flags each have an action, or the detector is not finished.
Every measurement is written up where anyone can read it: an experiment entry, a row in the decision ledger, and a comment on its issue.

instruments.name: Monthly corpus audit
instruments.question: On a random page, does the English say what the transcription says?
instruments.scope: About 100 books drawn at random each month, one interior page each, all languages

latest.headline: 14.3% of pages have a major error (95% CI 7.4–22.3)

instruments.on_finding: Defect classes become issues. Pages are not held automatically.
instruments.blind_to: The page image (a wrong leaf passes), page ends, and anything about the book as a whole

instruments.name: Image-and-book spot check
instruments.question: Read against the page image: is it the right page, is the reading right, is the English right, does the book belong where it is filed, may we publish it?
instruments.scope: 30 books drawn at random, 3 consecutive pages each, read against the images

latest.headline: 21 of 91 pages (23%) with a serious error; about 18 of 30 books with a defect visible on sight

instruments.on_finding: Broken and in-copyright books are hidden the same day; each defect class becomes an issue.
instruments.blind_to: Rates for single languages (30 books is too few)

instruments.name: Our English against published translations
instruments.question: Where a person has published a translation of the same passage, how close is ours?
instruments.scope: 321 pages in five language tracks (84000, SuttaCentral and others), two blind AI judges

latest.headline: Correcting the transcription lifts fidelity most (+0.65 to +1.77 on a 1–5 scale); the stronger model cuts reversed statements from 15 to 6 per 100 pages (Sanskrit, Pali, Chinese)

instruments.on_finding: Ranks the levers in the decision ledger; changes to models and prompts must beat it.
instruments.blind_to: Texts nobody has translated, which is most of what we hold

instruments.name: Our reading against typed editions
instruments.question: Where people have typed the same edition, how many characters did our reading get wrong, and what does that predict for pages with no typed edition?
instruments.scope: Kanripo (Chinese classics), CBETA, VRI (Pali); more editions to follow

latest.headline: Kanripo screen on the PaddleOCR reading: 6.6% of 992,881 pages flagged as disagreeing

instruments.on_finding: Flagged pages are listed; not yet held from translation (proposed in #5915).
instruments.blind_to: Genuine textual variants between editions, until the by-eye floor is measured

instruments.name: Page-integrity walk
instruments.question: Across every book: are pages missing, repeated or out of order, and is any translation cut short or a copy of the original?
instruments.scope: Every page in the corpus mirror, eight automatic checks

latest.headline: 20,933 page-number breaks in 6,472 books, about 45% real by a read of 20

instruments.on_finding: Repair lists only. Nothing yet holds a flagged book from view.
instruments.blind_to: Scans spliced from different copies where the numbering still runs

instruments.name: Page-error taxonomy
instruments.question: What kinds of thing go wrong on a page, named from pages opened and read?
instruments.scope: 44 defect classes across image, reading and translation
instruments.on_finding: Each class names its detector or issue.
instruments.blind_to: How often each class occurs (that is the audits' job)

instruments.name: Rights screen
instruments.question: Is this edition still in copyright where we publish it?
instruments.scope: Title pages and imprints read from our own transcription; first run on the canon shelves
instruments.cadence: per run; not yet at import

latest.headline: 49 of 1,571 visible canon-shelf books found to be modern editions in copyright; all hidden

instruments.on_finding: The book is hidden, with a reason that stops it being republished in bulk.
instruments.blind_to: Books with no transcribed front matter

instruments.name: Readers of the original
instruments.question: Asked of a person who reads the source language: does the English say what this page says?
instruments.scope: Pages from the monthly audit draw, one at a time, sent to volunteers who read the language
instruments.on_finding: Checks the AI judge: where a reader and the judge disagree, the judge's rates are corrected.

board._about: The improvement board: defect classes ranked by how often the latest random check met them, each with its owner and status. Rewritten every review cycle (#5914); a fix counts when the next window's rate falls.

gaps.gap: No person who reads the source language has yet checked our pages, so every judged rate rests on AI judges no human has calibrated.
High-precision flags (duplicate scans, a repeated page, a typed-edition disagreement) do not yet hold a public book or page from view.
There is no rights check at import: the importer treats every Internet Archive scan as public domain until someone looks.
Quality on texts with no typed edition and no human translation is unknown, not estimated.
Books are not checked as wholes: shelf membership and the wrong work under a title are found only by eye.
